title: Cubes in a cube: three paths, two settings
question: The n = 12 cube record came from hardening balls into cubes with the original (untuned) schedule. In 3D, at n = 9 to 14, how do harden, grow and rigid compare at the record's budget, with the original settings and with each method's 2D-tuned settings?
hypothesis: harden is the only path that gets below 2.93277 at n = 12 under either setting; at n = 9 all three reach Friedman's packing.
decision_rule: Same 'solved' metric as C04 (tightened run within 1e-9 of the best known value, 1e-5 if truncated, or below it). Report per n, method and setting. sa and pc are not implemented in 3D; the comparison is limited to the three gradient paths. If a tightened run beats a catalogue value it is certified as in C04.

amendments.change: Before the first run: 3D tightening takes minutes per packing, so in each cell only the best run is tightened, and only if it is within 1% of the best known value (or within 2e-3 of it).
